newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight interbank rate steady at 8.60/70 pct.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight interbank rate steady at 8.60/70 pct.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate was steady at 8.60/70 percent on Monday as market liquidity remained tight, dealers said.
"The market is still a bit short and there's no sign of Bank Negara lending on the overnight today," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
Earlier, interbank rates were also steady despite fresh injection of one-month funds by agent banks of Bank Negara, dealers said.
One-month money was at 8.50 percent against 8.40/50 percent on Friday.
Three-month money was steady at 8.30 percent.
"Bank Negara agents were lending a bit of money this morning but it was not enough to pull down rates. The market is still very tight," said one dealer.
Dealers said although some Bank Negara agents continued lending, the market was too short to prevent a spike up in rates.
They said merchant banks and finance companies continued to bid rates up.
Bank Negara is said to have injected funds over the past 10 days to help ease market tightness.
Recent heavy buying of the ringgit by the central bank to defend the currency from speculative attack had caused a liquidity squeeze.
There was no confirmation of the funds injection from Bank Negara, which does not usually comment on its market operations.
Dealers said rates would have gone up further but for a persistent rumour about a possible cut in banks' statutory reserves requirement (SRR).
Banks in Malaysia have to maintain a certain percentage of their deposits in liquid assets, mainly government paper.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange extended their fall to reflect the firmness in interbank rates, futures dealers said.
At 0900 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was down eight points to 92.24, or an implied yield of 7.76 percent.
The December contract fell five to 92.49, or 7.51 percent while March 1998 was down four to 92.58, or 7.42 percent.
